jobs.description: Directory | MyCU Home Search Jobs Log In /Create Account Help Concord University Home Human Resources Chamber of Commerce of the Two Virginias Employment Notices Adjunct Instructor of Mathematics Below you will find the details for the position including any supplementary documentation and questions you should review before applying for the opening. Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Please see Special Instructions for more details. Requirements for Completed Application.- Letter of application- CV- Unofficial copy of transcripts (The selected candidate will be required to submit official copies of transcripts before time of appointment- Three references and their contact information (including a current address, phone number and e-mail address) Posting Details Position Information Job Category Hourly/Adjunct Position Title Adjunct Instructor of Mathematics Working Title Adjunct Instructor of Mathematics Scheduled Hours Per Week FLSA Status Exempt Job Summary Job Summary Concord University’s Department of Mathematics and Computer Science invites applications for adjunct faculty positions in Mathematics.Adjunct instructors will teach introductory mathematics courses—including Quantitative Reasoning, College Algebra, and Elementary Statistics, as well as associated corequisite support sections. Courses may be offered in person on Concord University’s main campus in Athens, WV, and/or online, depending on departmental needs.. Successful candidates will demonstrate a commitment to high‑quality undergraduate instruction, support for student success in foundational mathematics, and alignment with Concord University’s mission of fostering academic excellence and a supportive learning environment. Applicants must hold a master’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, or a closely related field. Duties and Responsibilities Duty/Responsibility To perform this role successfully, an individual should be able to: Prepare and deliver instruction in introductory mathematics courses in alignment with the established course map, in both in‑person and online formats. Develop and maintain course materials, including syllabi, assignments, and supplemental instructional resources. Assess student learning through assignments, tests, and other evaluations, grading fairly and consistently, and providing timely feedback to support student progress. Contribute to General Education Assessment by collecting, documenting, and reporting required course data. Maintain regular office hours to provide academic support, assist with course‑related questions, and contribute to student recruitment and retention efforts. Keep accurate records of attendance, grades, and other required documentation in compliance with federal FERPA regulations. Perform additional duties as assigned by the Department Chair or Dean. % of Time 100 Education/Knowledge Minimum Education Master's Required Licenses/Certification Master’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, or a closely related field. Required Skills Solid understanding of introductory mathematics, including quantitative reasoning, algebra, and statistics Strong teaching and communication skills, with the ability to explain concepts clearly to a wide range of learners Ability to create a supportive and engaging learning environment Skill in developing instructional materials and using effective teaching strategies Proficiency with learning management systems and basic instructional technology Strong organizational abilities, including timely grading, accurate record‑keeping, and adherence to academic policies Ability to work effectively with faculty, staff, and students Commitment to Concord University’s mission and to supporting student success in foundational coursework Required Experience Type of experience Needed Experience teaching Quantitative Reasoning, College Algebra, and/or Elementary Statistics preferred Amount of Experience Needed (Months/Years) More than 2 years Posting Detail Information Close Date Open Until Filled Yes Additional Information Requirements for Completed Application.- Letter of application- CV- Unofficial copy of transcripts (The selected candidate will be required to submit official copies of transcripts before time of appointment- Three references and their contact information (including a current address, phone number and e-mail address) Quick Link to Posting https://jobs.concord.edu/postings/1602 Posting Supplemental Questions Required fields are indicated with an asterisk (*). Applicant Documents Required Documents Resume Cover Letter Optional Documents Unofficial Transcripts Concord University is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity employer. Women, minorities, veterans, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Concord University 1000 Vermillion Street P.O. Box 1000 Athens, West Virginia 24712-1000 1-800-344-6679 | 1-304-384-3115

jobs.title: Assistant Professor
jobs.description: Assistant Professor Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Position Details Get to Know Us! Marshall University is a public comprehensive university with a rich history as one of the oldest institutions of higher learning in West Virginia. Founded in 1837 and named after Chief Justice John Marshall, definer of the Constitution, Marshall University advances the public good through innovative, accredited educational programs. We are located in downtown Huntington, West Virginia, with additional locations in South Charleston, Point Pleasant, Teays Valley and Beckley. Marshall University’s mission, inspired by our Vision and Creed, includes a commitment to: Offer a wide range of high quality, affordable, and accessible undergraduate, graduate, and professional education that prepares students to think, learn, work, and live in an evolving global society. Create opportunities and experiences to foster understanding and appreciation of the rich diversity of thought and culture. Maintain a dynamic intellectual, artistic, and cultural life by promoting and supporting research and creative activities by undergraduates, graduates, and faculty. Contribute to the quality of life of the community, region, and beyond through applied research, economic development, health care, and cultural enrichment. Cultivate the development of an inclusive, just, and equitable community. Come Meet Marshall and discover what it means to be part of the Marshall University family! Come join our Herd! We are committed to attracting and retaining quality faculty and staff. In doing so, Marshall University offers outstanding benefit packages to eligible employees only. (E-Class in the job posting). Marshall University Research Corporation (MURC) employees have different benefit options than those listed below. Work week is 37.5 hrs. A great highlight in December is that Marshall University employees receive almost two weeks off for Winter Break! Holidays – Employees receive 13 Paid Holidays Annual and Sick Leave – Classified Staff, Non-Classified Staff and 12-month Faculty earn up to 24 days of annual leave per year (max 360 hours) and up to 18 days of sick leave per year. ) Employee Leave Health Insurance – Marshall University offers health insurance through West Virginia Public Employees Insurance Agency (PEIA). There are seven (7) health benefit plans. Educational/Tuition Benefits – Marshall University provides tuition benefits to regular employees (after probationary period) and their dependent children. Retirement Plans – Marshall University offers retirement through Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association (TIAA). Full-time benefits eligible employees must participate in the mandated retirement plan (401(a)). Life Insurance – Basic term life insurance ($10,000) at no cost and may purchase optional life insurance coverage with pre-tax earnings. Wellness Programs – PEIA provides various care management programs and the Pathways to Wellness program. We are . . . Marshall! Position Information Banner Position Number 000388 Position Title Assistant Professor Classification Title Assistant Professor Department Finance/Economics Department - MU2320 Job Description The Department of Finance, Economics, and International Business in the Lewis College of Business at Marshall University invites applications for a nine-month tenure-track Assistant Professor of Finance position beginning in Fall 2027. The Lewis College of Business, housed in the newly constructed, state-of-the-art Brad D. Smith Center for Business & Innovation, holds dual AACSB accreditation in both business and accounting. Marshall University is a Carnegie classified high-research activity institution located in Huntington, West Virginia, and is guided by its Marshall For All, Marshall Forever strategic vision, which emphasizes affordability, flexibility, and student achievement. The successful candidate will be expected to teach a variety of undergraduate and graduate finance courses in face-to-face, online, and hybrid formats. Additional teaching opportunities may be available in the College’s Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) program. Preference will be given to applicants with experience teaching Financial Markets and Institutions, Bank Management, and Derivatives and Risk Management. Location MU - Marshall University Salary Range Salary commensurate with experience and internal equity. Qualifications Must be able to perform all essential job duties as outlined in the job description. Required Qualifications Education Hold a Ph.D. in Finance from an AACSB-accredited business school. ABDs close to completion will be considered. Experience Demonstrate a strong record of, or potential for, high-quality scholarly research and a commitment to publishing in reputable peer-reviewed academic journals.Demonstrate excellence in teaching undergraduate and graduate finance courses, along with a strong commitment to student learning and success. Preferred Qualifications Education Experience Experience teaching with the Bloomberg Terminal.Experience supervising a student-managed investment fund. Position Information Banner Position Number 000387 Position Title Assistant Professor Classification Title Assistant Professor Department Accountancy/Legal Environment - MU2310 Job Description The Prentiss Lee Faulconer Jr. Department of Accountancy & Legal Environment at Marshall University is seeking an assistant professor for a nine-month tenure track appointment beginning Fall 2027 semester, with preference given to candidates who can begin Spring 2027 semester. The position will include teaching responsibilities at the undergraduate and graduate levels, with a willingness to work with DBA students.The primary need is in financial accounting, but applicants from all areas of accounting are welcome to apply. Candidates must possess the interest and/or demonstrated ability to teach using face-to-face, online, and hyflex delivery methods. Successful candidates need to demonstrate effective teaching ability, a potential for research that produces publications in high-quality peer-reviewed journals, and a commitment to participating in department, college, and university service. Marshall University is a Carnegie classified high-research activity institution located in Huntington, West Virginia. The Lewis College of Business has the distinction of being one of the fewer than 200 business schools worldwide that are accredited in both business and accounting by AACSB. In Spring 2024, the College moved into a new state-of-the-art facility known as the Brad D. Smith Center for Business & Innovation. The Mission of the Prentiss Lee Faulconer Jr. Department of Accountancy & Legal Environment is to provide an education that will enable graduates to successfully enter the profession of accountancy, business, and/or graduate study. The faculty is committed to maintaining a current and relevant curriculum in the fields of accountancy and legal environment through professional engagement, service to our communities, and the development of applied and pedagogical research.Earned Doctorate in Accounting or Business Administration with an Accounting concentration (Ph.D or DBA) Program from an AACSB-accredited institution. ABD candidates will be considered. Location MU - Marshall University Salary Range Salary is commensurate with qualifications, experience, and internal equity. Qualifications Must be able to perform all essential job duties as outlined in the job description. Required Qualifications Education Earned Doctorate in Accounting or Business Administration with an Accounting concentration (Ph.D or DBA) Program from an AACSB-accredited institution. ABD candidates will be considered. Experience Experience teaching accounting courses at a university level, with demonstrated above-average teaching ability and quality scholarly research. Preferred Qualifications Education Completed doctoral dissertation and defense; Terminal degree from AACSB-accredited institution. Experience CPA and significant professional accounting

The preferred candidate will have a terminal degree in Communication Sciences and Disorders or related field; will consider applicants with a master’s degree in communication disorders/speech-language pathology and hold the Certificate of Clinical Competence in SLP with a minimum of 5 years’ experience and have experience in at least one of the following areas: speech sound disorders, speech science, child language disorders and autism spectrum disorders. Additionally, the ideal candidate will contribute to the College’s support of interdisciplinary programs of study. Will include (not necessarily all) of the following: teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in the area of specialization and assigned by the Chair of the Department, supervising students on campus in the Marshall University Speech and Hearing Center and potentially outside contracts, engaging in scholarly activity and service to the department, college, and university at large.
